concept.body: A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides congruent. It inherits every parallelogram property and adds two diagonal powers: the diagonals are perpendicular, and each bisects its vertex angles. The diagonals cut the rhombus into four congruent right triangles whose legs are the HALF-diagonals and whose hypotenuse is the side.

explanationVariants: Half-diagonals 3 and 4 are the legs: side = √(9 + 16) = 5.
Diagonals 6 and 8 halve to 3 and 4 — the classic 3-4-5 gives side 5.

widget.prompt: A rhombus has diagonals 6 and 8. Its side = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 10 = √(6² + 8²) skipped the halving — the right triangles use HALF of each diagonal: √(3² + 4²) = 5.
7 = 3 + 4 adds the legs — they meet at 90°, so Pythagoras: √(9 + 16) = 5.

steps.body: The **rhombus** takes the other upgrade path: a parallelogram with **all four sides congruent** (one pair of congruent consecutive sides is enough to trigger it — opposite sides copy them). Angles stay free to lean; it's the SIDES that lock. Every rhombus keeps the full parallelogram toolkit.

explanationVariants: All four sides match, so the perimeter is 4 × 9 = 36.
One side of a rhombus prices them all: 4 × 9 = 36.

widget.prompt: One side of a rhombus measures 9. Its perimeter = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 18 = 2 × 9 doubles as if only OPPOSITE sides matched (a generic parallelogram needs two lengths). A rhombus has all four equal: 36.
81 = 9² computes an area-flavored square — perimeter ADDS the sides: 4 × 9 = 36.

steps.body: The rhombus's diagonals carry TWO new powers. They are **perpendicular**, and each one **bisects the vertex angles** it joins. (They still bisect each other — inherited.) The proof is the equal sides at work: each diagonal splits the rhombus into congruent isosceles triangles, SSS everywhere.

explanationVariants: The diagonal from a 70° vertex bisects it: 70 ÷ 2 = 35°.
Vertex-angle bisection is the rhombus diagonal's power: half of 70° is 35°.

widget.prompt: A rhombus has a 70° vertex angle. What angle does the diagonal from that vertex make with each of its two sides?

commonErrors.feedback: 70° keeps the whole vertex angle — the diagonal BISECTS it: 35° on each flank.
55 = (180 − 70)/2 halves the SUPPLEMENT — that's the neighboring vertex's half. This vertex splits 70: 35°.
20 = 90 − 70 subtracts from a right angle — no right angle sits at the vertex. Halve instead: 35°.

steps.body: Perpendicular + mutually bisecting diagonals slice a rhombus into **four congruent right triangles**, each with legs equal to HALF of each diagonal. Diagonals 12 and 16: legs 6 and 8, so each side — the hypotenuse — is √(36 + 64) = 10. Diagonals in, side out, via Pythagoras.

explanationVariants: Half-diagonals 6 and 8 are the legs: side = √(6² + 8²) = 10 — the 6-8-10 triple.
Halve both diagonals first, then Pythagoras: √(36 + 64) = 10.

widget.prompt: A rhombus has diagonals 12 and 16. Find its side length.

commonErrors.feedback: 20 = √(12² + 16²) forgot to HALVE the diagonals — the right triangles use half of each: √(6² + 8²) = 10.
14 = 6 + 8 adds the half-diagonals — they're perpendicular LEGS, so Pythagoras: √(36 + 64) = 10.
28 = 12 + 16 adds the full diagonals — neither halved nor squared. √(6² + 8²) = 10.

widget.prompt: Build a rhombus: four sides, two parallel pairs, and all four sides equal.
widget.successFeedback: A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides equal — no right angles required. Add four right angles as well and it becomes a square, which is why the square sits inside both families.
widget.sidesFeedback: Start inside the quadrilateral family with four sides.
widget.attributesFeedback: A rhombus needs all four sides equal, and it keeps the parallelogram's two parallel pairs.

widget.prompt: A rhombus's diagonals intersect. How many degrees in each angle at the crossing point?

commonErrors.feedback: 45° halves the right angle — the diagonals themselves CROSS at 90°; the 45s appear only in a square's corner halves.
60° would suit an equilateral-triangle fan — rhombus diagonals are perpendicular by theorem: 90°.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Perpendicular diagonals: all four crossing angles are 90°.

hints: The four congruent right triangles have hypotenuse 13 (the side) and one leg 5 (half the 10-diagonal).
The other leg is half the unknown diagonal: √(13² − 5²).
√(169 − 25) = √144 = 12 is the HALF — the question asks the full diagonal.
explanationVariants: Half-diagonal = √(13² − 5²) = 12, so the full diagonal is 24 — the 5-12-13 triple at work.
Hypotenuse 13, leg 5 → other leg 12 → double for the whole diagonal: 24.

widget.prompt: A rhombus has side 13 and one diagonal of length 10. Find the OTHER diagonal.

commonErrors.feedback: 12 is the HALF-diagonal (√(169 − 25)). Diagonals bisect each other — double it: 24.
26 = 2 × 13 doubles the SIDE — but the side is the hypotenuse of the half-diagonal triangle, not a half-diagonal itself. √(13² − 5²) = 12 per half → 24.
13.93 ≈ √(169 + 25) ADDS squares — but 13 is the hypotenuse, so its square is the total: √(169 − 25) = 12, doubled = 24.

takeaways: Rhombus = parallelogram + all sides congruent; perimeter = 4 × side.
Diagonals: perpendicular AND vertex-angle-bisecting (bisection of each other is inherited).
Half-diagonals + side form right triangles — Pythagoras converts between them.
steps.teaser: Next: what happens when BOTH upgrade paths fire at once — the square.
